title.en: Slot occupancy and undo integrity in a configurator

summary: Check that slot occupancy stays one-to-one, previews never commit, and undo restores occupancy and transforms together.
objective: Forward and reverse occupancy maps agree after every committed operation and after every undo.
applies_when: Accessories or modules mount into named slots with compatibility rules.
A candidate can be previewed before it is committed.
The interface offers undo, presets or saved configurations.
intent_signals: two accessories ended up in one slot
undo left the mesh but cleared the slot
example_prompts: Check the slot rules and undo behaviour of this camera rig configurator.

principles: A configurator is a small typed graph: each slot holds at most one attachment and each attachment has exactly one parent slot. Everything visual follows from those two statements.
A preview is not a commitment; an invalid candidate must never appear in the committed occupancy map, not even for one frame.
Undo restores occupancy and transforms together, because restoring one without the other produces a plausible picture over an inconsistent model.
implementation: Represent occupancy as a slot-to-attachment map plus its reverse, and recompute the reverse from the forward map after every committed operation.

Write down the history policy first, including whether entries are per commit or coalesced, whether depth is bounded, and whether a redo cursor and a saved baseline exist, because undo integrity can only be compared against a stated policy.

Run a fixed operation script instead of random clicking: mount A, mount B into the same slot, mount an incompatible accessory, mount a child onto a slot whose parent was removed, then undo three times.
After each step dump occupancy, each mounted transform and each mesh scene-graph parent, and compare the three descriptions with one another.
Include a candidate that is legal by slot type but illegal by geometry, so that the rule which rejected it is identified explicitly.
observable_checks: Forward and reverse occupancy maps agree after every committed operation, and every mounted mesh scene parent matches its recorded slot.

A rejected mount leaves occupancy, transforms and history unchanged, and the history matches the declared policy: one entry per commit under an unbounded per-commit policy, or the coalescing, bounded depth and baseline behaviour that policy actually specifies.
Each undo restores the occupancy and the transforms of the same step; a step that restores one but not the other is reported with its index.

known_limits: Checks model integrity of an authored compatibility table; it does not validate that the table describes any real product system.
Authored verification guidance; no interface was run for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.
